You make an attempt to remember things from the Great War, but remember almost nothing. response:
FADE IN:

INT. VETERAN'S BEDROOM - DAY

We see a small, cluttered bedroom. There's a bed, a dresser, and a few pieces of furniture scattered around. The walls are adorned with old photographs and war memorabilia. We see a WW1 veteran, JIM (60s), lying in bed, looking confused. He's dressed in a worn-out uniform, and his hair is thinning.

JIM
(to himself)
What's my name? What's my name?

He looks around the room, trying to remember something. Suddenly, he sees a photograph on the dresser.

JIM
(excitedly)
Oh, yes! I remember! I was at the front lines! I was with my unit...

He looks at the photograph, trying to recall the details. But his mind is a blank.

JIM
(frustrated)
No, no, no... I don't remember anything.

He looks around the room again, trying to find something to trigger his memory. He sees a small, leather-bound book on the nightstand.

JIM
(excitedly)
Ah, yes! My journal! I wrote about the war in this...

He opens the book, but it's filled with blank pages.

JIM
(disappointed)
No... no... I don't remember writing anything.

He looks up, and sees a man standing in the doorway. It's a young man, probably in his early 20s.

JIM
(confused)
Who are you?

MAN
Hi, Mr. Jim. My name is John. I'm a nurse.

JIM
(confused)
Nurse? What do you mean?

MAN
You're a veteran, Mr. Jim. You were in the war.

JIM
(confused)
War? What war?

MAN
World War I.

JIM
(confused)
No... no... I don't remember anything.

The man looks at Jim with concern.

MAN
It's okay, Mr. Jim. You're not alone. We can help you remember.

JIM
(skeptical)
Remember? What do you mean?

MAN
You have dementia, Mr. Jim. You're not remembering things because of the war.

JIM
(confused)
Dementia? What's that?

MAN
It's a condition where your brain doesn't work properly.

JIM
(confused)
My brain? What's wrong with my brain?

MAN
You're not remembering things because of the trauma you experienced during the war.

JIM
(confused)
Trauma? What trauma?

MAN
You were in the trenches, Mr. Jim. You saw things that no one should ever have to see.

JIM
(confused)
Trenches? What trenches?

MAN
You were in the front lines, Mr. Jim. You were fighting for your country.

JIM
(confused)
Country? What country?

MAN
England.

JIM
(confused)
England? No... no... I don't remember anything.

The man looks at Jim with sadness.

MAN
It's okay, Mr. Jim. We'll help you remember.

JIM
(suddenly)
Wait! I remember something!

MAN
What is it, Mr. Jim?

JIM
(excitedly)
I remember looking to my side... and seeing a man get shot in the head...

He looks at the man, who looks shocked.

MAN
Mr. Jim, that's not possible. You were in the war, but you didn't see anything like that.

JIM
(confused)
What do you mean? I remember it like it was yesterday.

MAN
Mr. Jim, you need to calm down. You're not remembering things correctly.

JIM
(frustrated)
No, no, no... I remember it! I remember the man's brains falling out from the back of his head!

The man looks at Jim with concern.

MAN
Mr. Jim, that's not possible. You need to calm down.

JIM
(confused)
What's going on? What's happening to me?

The man tries to calm Jim down, but Jim becomes more and more agitated.

FADE TO BLACK.
